points: Q3 2026 will test whether the Q2 record revenue of $448.8 million, up 14.9% year over year, and the raised full-year 2026 guidance reflected durable screening volume or one-time tailwinds; the 8/0 upward revision ratio already assumes the beat continues.
The Nov. 5 print will reveal if management can sustain the raised 2026 outlook through Q4, given consensus FY1 EPS growth of 22.7% and FY2 growth of 18.0% imply a strong second-half ramp.
With revenue estimates up 4.09% over the past 90 days and no estimate cuts, the market is pricing operating leverage from the Q2 beat to carry into Q3 and Q4.
Peer prints from PAYX on Oct. 18 and RHI on Nov. 3 will provide real-time read-throughs on U.S. hiring and screening demand before FA reports; weaker peer guidance would challenge the long case.
Valuation is supportive for the long: FA trades at 16.4x FY1 earnings and a 0.72 PEG, or roughly 0.8x the theme median P/E, leaving room if growth stays above 20%.
The HR & Employment Services theme is cold and breadth is flat, so the long case depends on company-specific execution rather than group momentum.

Q4 2026 setup hinges on the Q3 call's guidance and commentary; the raised full-year outlook likely requires Q4 to remain at least as strong as Q2, and any Q4 caution would put FY2 EPS of $1.51 at risk.
watch: Q3 2026 revenue growth year over year: staying near or above Q2's 14.9% supports the long.
FY2026 guidance trajectory: maintaining or raising the post-Q2 outlook supports the long; a cut undermines it.
Q4 2026 implied guidance and commentary: a strong Q4 setup is needed to justify FY2 EPS growth of 18.0%.
Peer demand signals from PAYX and RHI before FA prints: stable or improving hiring/backdrop supports the long.
